checked_sources.source: Tianyi Ma, Hanzhang Qin, Ruihao Zhu, Jierui Zuo, Best-Arm Identification with Generative Proxy, arXiv:2607.06879v1, 2026
checked_sources.result: Primary-verified the real-data replay numbers that were previously only partly verified. With delta=0.05, kappa=1.0 and 3,000 replay repetitions, reward-only PROBE stopped at 105.2k pulls mean (105.2k median, 106.7k 90th percentile). Qwen2.5-7B local ICL stopped at 101.7k (3.3% saving; |rho_hist|=0.275, |rho_imp|=0.011); GPT-5.5 API ICL at 95.6k (9.1%; 0.264, 0.327); Qwen2.5-7B LoRA at 52.0k (50.5%; 0.725, 0.707); TabPFN at 40.6k (61.4%; 0.822, 0.760). All variants were correct in all 3,000 repetitions. The same paper shows the calibration overhead is real: on the synthetic Gaussian instance proxy-assisted PROBE is worse than reward-only at rho=0 and only overtakes the no-proxy baseline once rho>=0.4 in that tested setup.

checked_sources.source: Le Yang, Vincent Y. F. Tan, Wang Chi Cheung, Best Arm Identification with Possibly Biased Offline Data, UAI 2025 / PMLR 286
checked_sources.result: Strengthened the exact safety boundary for historical evidence. LUCB-H requires a valid per-arm bias bound V(i)>=|mu_on(i)-mu_off(i)| and combines online-only and history-assisted intervals conservatively. Its stated expected stopping-time upper bound equals the online LUCB order minus a nonnegative saving term; when eta(i)=V(i)+mu_off(i)-mu_on(i) <= Delta_i/4, history can reduce sample complexity, otherwise the algorithm can fall back to standard LUCB order. The paper's misspecification appendix reports mild underestimation on suboptimal arms (V=0.1 or 0.15 vs true discrepancy 0.2) remained stable in one tested group because the best-arm bound was not underestimated; when all arms including the best arm use underestimated bounds, LUCB-H can be misled and underperform pure LUCB. Extreme V=0 fully trusts history and is especially dangerous for a biased true best arm. Screenshot retrieval for the PDF failed due cache miss; claims here are limited to text-extracted primary content.

checked_sources.source: Wang Chi Cheung, Lixing Lyu, Leveraging (Biased) Information: Multi-armed Bandits with Offline Data, ICML 2024 / PMLR 235
checked_sources.result: Independent adjacent confirmation of the same information-theoretic boundary in cumulative-regret bandits: without any non-trivial upper bound on offline-online discrepancy, no non-anticipatory policy can outperform vanilla UCB in general; with a valid bias bound, MIN-UCB adaptively chooses the tighter online-only versus history-assisted optimism and retains UCB-order behavior when history is misleading while improving when it is informative. This does not solve online learning of an unknown safe bias bound; it reinforces that such a guarantee is impossible without added structure.

checked_sources.source: Soonhui Lee, Barry L. Nelson, General-purpose ranking and selection for computer simulation, IISE Transactions 48(6), 2016
checked_sources.result: General-purpose R&S uses bootstrap inference rather than assuming a particular output family, supports different performance measures/distribution families and has separate CRN/non-CRN variants. It adds adaptive sample allocation to reduce the computational burden and establishes asymptotic PCS under mild conditions with finite-sample empirical evaluation. Exact finite-sample sample-saving ratios were not available in the accessible primary text, so this remains promising_unverified quantitatively rather than a strong candidate.

checked_sources.source: Christopher M. Healey, Sigrun Andradottir, Seong-Hee Kim, A minimal switching procedure for constrained ranking and selection under independent or common random numbers, IIE Transactions 47(11), 2015
checked_sources.result: Useful negative guardrail for common-random-number evaluation: CRN can significantly reduce samples, but comparing systems with unequal sample counts can lose the intended probability-of-correct-selection guarantee. The authors introduce variance-estimate corrections that restore good PCS at the cost of additional observations. This directly constrains adaptive seed/scenario reuse: paired/covariance-aware comparisons must preserve pairing semantics or use corrected variance estimators.

candidates_new.mechanism: When candidate-evaluation output distribution or performance metric is not trustworthy enough for a parametric confidence model, use bootstrap-based ranking-and-selection with adaptive sample allocation, optionally preserving common-random-number dependence, rather than forcing Gaussian/light-tail assumptions.
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: Primary accessible text establishes asymptotic PCS under mild conditions and reports finite-sample empirical evaluation, but exact headline sample-reduction numbers were not recovered in this run. Do not promote to a strong quantitative mechanism until those ratios or a newer open primary benchmark are extracted.
candidates_new.operational_observable: Track attained PCS/PGS on calibration problems, bootstrap interval coverage, per-candidate sample allocation, resampling compute cost, and result stability versus a parametric R&S shadow path. For CRN, also track pairing completeness and covariance-estimator validity.
candidates_new.scope: Simulation ranking-and-selection across heterogeneous output distributions/performance measures. Asymptotic guarantee plus empirical finite-sample evidence; not a universal finite-sample exact guarantee for arbitrary heavy tails.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: Bootstrap computation can dominate if resampling is expensive; finite-sample calibration may be poor for rare-event/extreme-tail targets. Under CRN, unequal sample counts can invalidate naive covariance comparisons unless pairing/variance corrections are used.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Research systems should switch from parametric confidence allocation to a bootstrap/general-purpose evaluation mode when output-family assumptions become suspect, while explicitly measuring calibration and preserving scenario-pairing semantics.

evidence_updates.update: Primary-verified the previously secondary-only auto-loan result. Reward-only mean stopping time was 105.2k pulls. TabPFN cut it to 40.6k (61.4%) with armwise absolute correlations 0.822/0.760; LoRA cut it to 52.0k (50.5%) with 0.725/0.707. Weak proxies gave only 3.3% and 9.1% savings. All variants were correct in 3,000/3,000 replay repetitions. Synthetic evidence also gives an explicit admission guardrail: at rho=0 PROBE pays overhead; in the tested Gaussian instance it only beats reward-only once rho>=0.4.

The valid-bias-bound requirement is stronger than an implementation detail: LUCB-H (fixed-confidence identification) and MIN-UCB (regret minimization) both have impossibility results showing that without non-trivial discrepancy information, a generally better-than-target-only policy is unavailable. LUCB-H supplies a concrete useful-history condition eta(i)<=Delta_i/4 and a misspecification failure mode: underestimating the bound on the true best arm can make history-assisted learning worse than pure online LUCB.

Added a correctness guardrail from constrained R&S: common random numbers can reduce samples but naive comparisons with unequal replication counts can lose PCS validity. Adaptive scenario reuse should either keep paired samples aligned or use variance estimators explicitly corrected for unequal/partially paired samples.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Learn an arbitrary source-target bias magnitude online from target samples and still guarantee finite-sample no-worse-than-target-only behavior for every adversarial source without any prior structural information
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Still unsupported and now reinforced as impossible in two adjacent sequential objectives. UAI 2025 BAI and ICML 2024 regret results both require a non-trivial valid discrepancy/bias bound for robust guaranteed improvement over online-only baselines.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: The exact frontier should shift from searching for a structure-free solution to identifying the weakest auditable structural information that can produce a valid bound: paired proxy residual certificate, target validation split, invariant features, causal constraints, or distribution-shift upper confidence bounds.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Maintain a reward-only shadow/admission gate and measure realized same-unit correlation or certified residual-variance gain before committing expensive sampling budget to proxy calibration.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Common-random-number scenario reuse remains statistically valid under arbitrary adaptive unequal sample counts

deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Scenario reuse requires pairing-aware inference, not just positive empirical covariance.
